Spain-United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income (1990, as amended by 2013 Protocol)
Spain-Latin America DTAA network (Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Argentina and Peru) covering royalties, audiovisual services and translation activities relevant to the LatAm bridge strategy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Real Decreto-ley 7/2021 and transposing EU Directives 2015/849, (EU) 2018/843 and (EU) 2018/1673; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, implementing regulation; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital, Articles 177-182 on UBO disclosure duties; Central Register of Real Titularities (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales) administered through notarial and commercial registry filings

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Good Standing Certificate or Certified Registry Extract of any corporate shareholder (Certificado de Registro)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or other competent corporate registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and Apostilled Power of Attorney (Poder Notarial) appointing the Spanish formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin of the UBO or sole shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Passport or National Identity Document of every Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish consular office or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Disclosure and Holding Structure Declaration (Declaración de Titular Real)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate beneficial owners, submitted before the incorporating Spanish notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed as a Spanish notarial instrument; no apostille required in the domestic incorporation deed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter or Source-of-Funds Evidence from the UBO's existing financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled or consularly legalized and accompanied by sworn translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All identified UBOs, proposed directors, and authorized signatories are screened before incorporation against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU autonomous sanctions (Council Regulations (EU) No 2580/2001 and No 881/2002), the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, and Spanish national vigilance data maintained by the Secretaría de Estado de Seguridad and the Banco de España. Persons holding prominent public functions during the last 12 months, together with family members and close associates, are classified as PEPs and subjected to enhanced due diligence. The compliance file must document source of funds, source of wealth, and a negative sanctions-hit result for each UBO and director, following the SEPBLAC risk-assessment model and the obligations under Law 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Sede Electrónica del Registro Mercantil Central - Solicitud de Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social (https://sede.registromercantil.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be written in Latin script using Spanish orthographic rules; Spanish diacritics (á, é, í, ó, ú, ñ) are permitted. Non-Spanish Latin-script names are admissible if phonetically and visually distinct from existing Spanish denominations. Purely non-Latin scripts must be fully transliterated into Latin equivalents before registration. The full legal form name must include 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.'
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Official or quasi-official references: 'España', 'Estado', 'Gobierno', 'Ministerio', 'Casa Real', 'Banco de España', 'ONU', 'UE', 'OTAN' (prior ministerial authorization required)
Regulated financial terms: 'Banco', 'Seguros', 'Sociedad de Inversión', 'Fondos', 'Entidad de Crédito' (prior Banco de España or DGSFP authorization required)
Terms contrary to law, morality or public order, and misleading terms creating confusion with public institutions or registered public trademarks
Territorial denominations of Spanish Autonomous Communities or municipalities when used as the sole distinctive element without proper authorization
Protected professional or civil titles such as 'Colegio', 'Consejo General', 'Asociación Profesional' in a manner suggesting an official body
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a negative certification or rejection, the applicant may either (a) re-submit a new application with up to three alternative names ranked by preference, or (b) file a recurso de alzada within one month from the rejection notice before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice, submitted through the Registro Mercantil Central. A subsequent recurso contencioso-administrativo may be lodged before the Audiencia Nacional. The name certificate expires after 90 days and is not extendable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for an ISIC 7490 localization agency only when the virtual office provider supplies a physical street address in the municipality of the registered office, statutory mail forwarding and notice handling, and the company demonstrates economic substance through its Spanish bank account, VAT registration, invoicing and management functions. Purely electronic or P.O.-box addresses are rejected by the Registro Mercantil and AEAT and are incompatible with Spanish tax-residence maintenance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Moderate - approximately 15% probability within the first 24 months of operation for a low-risk AML-tier agency; unannounced inspections are most plausible by AEAT for VAT and tax-residence checks and by Registro Mercantil inspectors when the registered office is a densified virtual office address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the incorporation deed in the Provincial Commercial Registry and BORME notification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) of Madrid
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registry tariff based on nominal capital and number of filing entries

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication in the Official Gazette of the Commercial Registry (BORME)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: BORME - Ministry of Justice electronic gazette
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; free electronic publication after registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial UBO declaration (Declaración de Titular Real) and AML/KYC compliance dossier

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 19-23, 28-32, 43-55, 61-63, 159-197, 210-241, and 278; Law 18/2022 on the Creation and Growth of Companies, including its amendments to minimum capital and formation procedures; Commercial Registry Regulations approved by Royal Decree 1784/1996.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, coordinated nationally through the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry, together with the prescribed registration application and tax identification documentation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until the capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders have supplementary liability for the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital in specified liquidation circumstances. A separate escrow account is not generally mandatory; a bank deposit certificate may be used, although the founders may instead assume joint responsibility for the accuracy of the contribution under Article 62 of the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscription and full payment of its issued share capital by [Founder Name], as recorded in the deed of incorporation. RESOLVED, that the registered office is adopted at [Full Spanish Address], with authority to update the address in the Commercial Registry when legally required. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed sole director for the statutory term, with the powers permitted by law and the articles of association, and is authorized to obtain the Company’s tax identification number, open bank accounts, execute filings, and complete all incorporation, employment, licensing, and operational formalities. The resolution is approved and signed by the attending shareholder(s) and director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), including its online name-certificate service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names and request the negative certificate of company name (certificación negativa de denominación social). Use the exact certified name in the deed and subsequent tax and registry filings. Foreign founders should provide notarized and, where applicable, apostilled powers of attorney with sworn Spanish translations.
required_dossiers: NIE or applicable foreigner identification documentation
Power of attorney, if filed by a representative
Sworn Spanish translation and apostille or legalization, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternative name or correct the objection and refile. The certificate is generally valid for three months for execution of the deed and six months for name reservation, subject to applicable registry rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Articles, Capital and Beneficial Ownership Information
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (Notario) and, where used, a Point of Attention to Entrepreneurs (Punto de Atención al Emprendedor) through the CIRCE system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association, registered office, corporate purpose, capital structure, share allocations, governance model, director details, and beneficial ownership declaration. Obtain evidence of capital payment if using a bank certificate, or include the founders’ statutory declaration accepting contribution liability. Ensure the corporate purpose covers translation, localization, audiovisual dubbing, subtitling, and related professional services.
required_dossiers: Founders’ passports or national identity documents
Bank deposit certificate or statutory contribution declaration
Registered office evidence or address details
Powers of attorney and sworn translations, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct documentary deficiencies identified by the notary. Amend the articles or corporate purpose before execution. If a founder lacks a NIE or acceptable identification, obtain the document before signing or use a properly notarized representative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public selected by the founders or CIRCE-appointed notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the public deed of incorporation in Spanish or with an authorized interpreter. The notary verifies identity, capacity, name reservation, capital, articles, beneficial ownership, and director appointment. Confirm that the deed expressly identifies the subscribed shares, paid-up capital, registered office, corporate purpose, governance system, and acceptance of office by directors.
required_dossiers: Capital payment evidence or statutory declaration
Apostilled powers and sworn translations, if relevant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure notarial observations before signature. If execution is refused, request the legal basis in writing, correct the deed or supporting documents, and reschedule execution. A notarial refusal may be challenged through the applicable Spanish notarial review process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification and Register the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT), followed by the competent Provincial Commercial Registry; CIRCE may transmit filings electronically
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the provisional NIF using Form 036 or the CIRCE process, file the incorporation deed with the Provincial Commercial Registry, and obtain the registry entry and definitive NIF. Submit the deed and required tax forms electronically where available. The company becomes fully operative as a registered legal person upon registration, subject to the legal effects of the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Registry application and proof of payment of registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a Commercial Registry qualification notice by correcting the deed or filing within the stated period. Resubmit the corrected document and obtain a new registry entry. If necessary, appeal the registrar’s qualification to the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith or the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Social Security and Economic Activity Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT, Treasury General of Social Security (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social), and the relevant municipal authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the definitive census registration and applicable economic activity classification with AEAT, register as an employer before hiring personnel, and enroll directors or workers in the appropriate Social Security regime. Register the business premises with the municipality if required and submit any responsible declaration for opening or activity commencement.
required_dossiers: Municipal responsible declaration or activity filing, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected census or Social Security filings within the notified deadline. Appeal or request review of municipal activity requirements from the issuing municipality. Do not commence regulated premises activity until the applicable declaration, permit, or inspection requirement is satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Post-Incorporation Governance and Compliance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company governing body, with filings before the Provincial Commercial Registry and other competent authorities where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the corporate books, record the shareholder register, approve banking authorities, adopt accounting and data-protection procedures, and document the first board or shareholder resolutions. Maintain the share ledger, minutes book, annual accounts, beneficial ownership information, and powers of attorney. File annual accounts and applicable changes of directors, registered office, corporate purpose, or share ownership.
required_dossiers: Annual accounts and management report, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify defective corporate records through a properly convened resolution and, where necessary, a corrective deed. Late annual accounts or governance filings should be regularized promptly to avoid registry closure, fines, or director liability exposure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ordinary professional translation, localization, subtitling, and media-dubbing services. The relevant municipality may require an activity declaration or operating authorization for the premises. The competent autonomous-community industrial authority may become relevant only if the business installs regulated industrial equipment or operates a facility subject to sector-specific rules.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific manufacturing or industrial operating permit is ordinarily required. Depending on the premises and municipality, the applicable instrument may be a municipal responsible declaration for commencement of activity (declaración responsable de inicio de actividad) or a municipal activity and opening license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), together with the competent environmental authority of the relevant autonomous community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt or not applicable for office-based translation and localization services under Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment. A project-specific screening is required if construction, major alteration, significant noise, industrial equipment, or an activity listed in the statutory annexes is proposed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific wastewater or VOC limits normally apply to office-based services. Any discharge must comply with the applicable municipal sewer ordinance and authorization conditions. Waste must be segregated and transferred through authorized waste managers under Law 7/2022 on Waste and Contaminated Soils. Dubbing studios must control acoustic emissions under applicable national, autonomous-community, and municipal noise rules. If solvents, generators, or other regulated equipment are introduced, additional air-emission, hazardous-waste, or industrial permitting may apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupying premises, obtain the applicable municipal activity or opening authorization and satisfy fire-safety requirements under the Spanish Building Technical Code and, where applicable, Royal Decree 2267/2004 on fire safety in industrial establishments. Structural load and installation inspections are required where the premises are altered or equipment is installed. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, including risk assessment, emergency planning, worker training, health surveillance where appropriate, and coordination with external prevention services. Additional acoustic or fire inspections may apply to recording and dubbing studios.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es). In the Basque Country and Navarra the devolved Foral Haciendas administer corporate income tax, but AEAT retains exclusive national competence for VAT, customs, and excise duties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Execute the SL incorporation deed before a Spanish notary, with the managing director already holding a Spanish NIE; 2) submit the census filing (Form 036 - Declaración censal) to AEAT, providing shareholder and manager details, the CNAE/ISIC 7490 activity code, and the registered office, which generates the provisional NIF; 3) register the company in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) within one month of incorporation; 4) upon certification of the registry inscription, AEAT converts the provisional NIF into the definitive CIF/NIF (letter plus eight digits plus control character, format N-12345678-0) through a supplementary Form 036 filing; 5) the VAT identification (NIF-IVA) and the IAE municipal business tax registration are embedded in the same census declaration; 6) non-resident shareholders must obtain NIF-N (foreign legal entity) or NIE (foreign individual), appoint a fiscal representative with power of attorney when required, and present apostilled foreign documents accompanied by an official sworn translation into Spanish.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a Spanish SL is an opaque resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) on worldwide income; the standard IS rate is 25% in mainland Spain, reduced to 15% for newly created entities with positive net equity in their first two tax periods (art. 29.1 LIS), with a 4% IS rate available to ZEC-qualifying entities in the Canary Islands and a 19% dividend/interest withholding generally applicable to non-resident shareholders under the Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR). No territorial or remittance-based carve-out applies to a resident SL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no check-the-box or pass-through election: an SL is permanently opaque, with no US-style entity classification election. Applicable statutory options include: (i) group taxation under the consolidated fiscal regime (LIS arts. 58-64) where direct/indirect control of 75% or more exists, elected through the corresponding tax-group census filing with AEAT; (ii) the automatic 15% reduced IS rate for qualifying newly created entities; (iii) the ETVE holding regime (art. 21 LIS) when the SL qualifies as a foreign-securities holding entity; (iv) the patent/innovation box allowing a 60% exemption of qualifying intangible income (art. 23 LIS); and (v) VAT grouping (grupo de entidades) for established Spanish group members. Hybrid mismatch rules transposing ATAD 2 (art. 15 LIS as amended by Ley 4/2021) override any cross-border mismatch election and invalidate double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), governed by Ley 37/1992 and RD 1624/1992; the Canary Islands apply IGIC (standard rate 7%, reduced 3%) and Ceuta/Melilla apply IPSI as separate indirect tax systems outside mainland Spanish VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general SME exemption or VAT registration threshold exists: any person commencing commercial, professional, or artistic activities must file Form 036/037 and obtain the NIF-IVA before the first supply, regardless of expected turnover or loss position; Spain has not transposed the EU cross-border small-business exemption into Ley 37/1992, and the simplified 'módulos' regime covers only listed retail, agriculture, and artisan activities, never professional localization services. In practice, the first B2B invoice triggers compulsory VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing is being phased in under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), with the implementing decree expected to require large undertakings (turnover over EUR 8,000,000) to issue, transmit, and receive structured e-invoices within one year of its approval and all other businesses within two years (expected compliance window 2025-2026); large enterprises and VAT groups subject to the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) must transmit invoice-issue and invoice-receipt records to AEAT via authenticated web services/API within 4 working days, with the extension to 8 calendar days for several record types, using XML/Facturae or EDIFACT formats; 'Verifactu' (RD 1007/2023 and Ley 11/2021 anti-fraud legislation) requires certified billing software that generates an immutable, hashed invoice record (Registro de Facturación), QR verification codes, and tamper-evident digital files; the Basque Country imposes the TicketBAI digital-stamping regime; invoices to Spanish public authorities must be submitted to the FACE portal as signed Facturae XML.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical export of goods: 0% export exemption under art. 21.1 Ley 37/1992 when a customs export declaration (DUA/Documento Único Administrativo) is accepted by AEAT customs and the goods physically leave the EU customs territory, evidenced by customs MRN status codes; goods must exit within the customs-supervised outward movement window (ordinarily 90 days from declaration acceptance, extendable with customs authorization). Localization services (translation, interpretation, subtitling, dubbing, transcreation) are services, not goods exports: zero-rating does not apply; instead the place-of-supply rules (arts. 69-70 LIVA) determine non-taxability as follows: (i) B2B services supplied to a customer established outside Spain are outside Spanish VAT scope, EU customers being subject to reverse charge with VIES VAT-number validation and non-EU customers bearing no Spanish VAT; (ii) B2C electronically supplied services (digital subtitle/master files) are deemed supplied at the consumer's location, so intra-EU consumer sales must be reported through the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) at destination-country VAT, with optional use of the EUR 10,000 intra-EU annual small-business threshold; (iii) input VAT attributable to non-taxable offshore services is recoverable only on a pro-rata basis (art. 104 LIVA) and, if the SL is not the exporter of goods, no customs export bundle applies to pure remote services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/Documento Único Administrativo) with MRN and customs exit status, lodged through AEAT's customs single window (Ventanilla Única Aduanera) or EDIFACT channel
Transportation and shipping evidence - Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or signed CMR as applicable, proving physical cross-border exit from EU territory

Commercial invoice incorporating INCOTERM, HS code, and the express clause 'exempt export - art. 21 Ley 37/1992' for goods, or for intra-EU supplies the VAT-registration references and 'reverse charge' indication

Inward Remittance Certificate from the payment rail (SWIFT MT103/MT202, Wise_B2B payout record, or Payoneer statement) evidencing receipt of foreign-currency export proceeds, adopting the 180-day inward-remittance compliance standard

Place-of-supply service documentation for localization work - signed localization/LMA contract, service acceptance certificate (dubbing QC report or translation delivery record), VIES validation printout for EU counterparties, and official sworn translation into Spanish where required

Ancillary media-delivery export file when physical deliverables (hard drives, master tapes, reference DVDs) are shipped, including packing list, freight forwarder receipt, and customs exit proof, archived with AEAT for the full 4-year limitation period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT has a 4-year statutory assessment period (art. 66 LGT). Wrongful zero-rating or export exemption is prosecuted as 'obtención indebida de devoluciones' and 'infracción por dejar de ingresar' under arts. 191-193 LGT, with proportional penalties ranging from 50% for simple negligence up to 150% for concealment or fraudulent documentation, plus late-payment interest computed at the statutory rate and retrospective VAT clawback recomputed at 21% over the full invoiced consideration. Failure to produce the customs DUA or exit proof automatically disqualifies the 0% rate and recharacterizes the supply as standard-rated. Fabrication of export documentation may trigger criminal tax evasion under art. 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, carrying imprisonment and fines. AEAT cross-border service audits combine the Verifactu/SII electronic invoice records with FX rail statements (Wise_B2B, Payoneer) to verify end-to-end traceability of exported services, and the burden of proof rests on the taxable person to substantiate the offshore destination and receipt of funds within the documented period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem and subject to applicable European Union payment-services, anti-money-laundering, capital-movement, and financial-markets rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and benefits from full current-account and capital-account convertibility under European Union law. There is no general Spanish exchange control, capital repatriation restriction, or requirement to obtain prior approval for ordinary inbound equity, intercompany loans, service receipts, dividends, interest, royalties, or liquidation proceeds. Transfers remain subject to bank identification, beneficial-owner verification, sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering controls, tax compliance, transfer-pricing support, and documentary evidence of the underlying transaction. Dividend, interest, royalty, and service remittances may trigger Spanish withholding-tax, treaty, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, or reporting analysis. Certain foreign investments may require ex post or prior declarations, and exceptional foreign-investment screening can apply to protected sectors or qualifying investors; a multilingual localization agency ordinarily falls outside protected-sector restrictions unless its facts create a regulated technology, defense, critical-infrastructure, or sensitive-data nexus.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, mandatory repatriation rule, compulsory conversion ratio, or fixed deadline for converting foreign-currency export receipts into euros. Export and service proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the company's discretion. Banks may request invoices, contracts, delivery evidence, customer identification, tax information, and payment-purpose data. Cross-border transactions may be reportable through Banco de España statistical-information systems or other regulatory channels depending on transaction type, resident status, amount, financial institution reporting, and applicable filing rules. Export receivables should be reconciled to accounting records, VAT treatment, customer invoices, and transfer-pricing documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection, supplier payments, foreign-currency wallets, and routine cross-border transfers, provided the provider is an authorized European Economic Area payment institution or electronic-money institution, or operates lawfully through passporting or an approved local arrangement. Wise Business, Payoneer, and comparable providers should be used only within their licensed product scope. They are not substitutes for a Spanish operating bank where a local corporate IBAN, statutory capital deposit, payroll, tax direct debit, cash services, bank guarantees, commercial lending, or enhanced documentary review is required. Client funds must not be commingled with company funds, and the company must not provide regulated payment, money-remittance, deposit-taking, or foreign-exchange services to third parties without authorization. Offshore digital EMI accounts may be rejected by Spanish counterparties, payment processors, auditors, or tax authorities where local account ownership, Spanish IBAN functionality, or resident-entity verification is required.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available through qualified electronic identification, video identification, notarized or apostilled documents, and electronic signature. In practice, the bank may require a branch visit, live video interview, Spanish-resident representative, or in-person verification where the shareholder chain is foreign, the entity is newly incorporated, the business is cross-border, the source of funds is complex, the directors are non-resident, or the proposed activity involves elevated payment flows. At least one authorized signatory and all ultimate beneficial owners should be prepared to complete enhanced verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SL with no operating history, no Spanish trading counterparties, and immediate international payment activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and current commercial-register extract; articles of association; tax identification number; director and signatory resolutions; business plan; signed customer and supplier contracts; invoices and pipeline evidence; expected monthly transaction volumes; countries, currencies, and counterparties; projected cash-flow statement; explanation of the localization and media-dubbing services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque non-resident ownership chain, nominee shareholder, trust, bearer-like arrangement, or inability to identify the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; corporate-register extracts for all intermediate entities; shareholder agreements; powers of attorney; trust or foundation documents where applicable; beneficial-owner declarations; Spanish beneficial-ownership filing evidence where applicable; independent legal confirmation of control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital or shareholder funding inconsistent with stated business size, unexplained third-party funding, or funds received from a high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed shareholder loan or equity-injection agreement; board and shareholder approvals; bank statements; audited or management accounts of the funding entity; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds memorandum; tax returns or financial statements; proof of ownership of the remitting account; payment purpose; sanctions and adverse-media screening; foreign-investment filing analysis where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border collections involving Latin America, offshore payment platforms, virtual assets, cash, or multiple unrelated remitters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer master file; signed service agreements; invoice-to-payment reconciliation; delivery and acceptance records; platform statements; counterparty KYC; transaction-monitoring policy; sanctions-screening procedure; prohibition on cash and virtual-asset settlement unless separately approved; explanation of payment aggregators and beneficial recipients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared ISIC 7490 localization activity and account behavior, including marketplace activity, payroll intermediation, lending, payment processing, or regulated audiovisual operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed activity memorandum; service catalog; website and client materials; sample statements of work; staffing model; subcontractor agreements; confirmation that the company acts as principal service provider rather than payment intermediary; applicable intellectual-property and data-processing documentation; licensing analysis confirming that no sectoral authorization is required for the stated activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete Spanish tax, accounting, VAT, payroll, or beneficial-ownership records, or failure to explain recurring transfers to related parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish tax registration; VAT status; accounting ledger; annual accounts; payroll records where relevant; related-party register; transfer-pricing policy; intercompany agreements; withholding-tax analysis; board approvals; reconciled bank statements; evidence of timely tax filings and payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, fraud, corruption, or restricted-country exposure involving a customer, director, shareholder, translator, subcontractor, or beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Risk-based enhanced due-diligence report; identity and ownership verification; sanctions-screening results; source-of-wealth evidence; contract and invoice rationale; compliance certifications; escalation and approval record; termination or blocking evidence where the relationship cannot be satisfactorily cleared.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity contributions and shareholder loans from an account held in the investor's own name to the Spanish SL's account at a regulated bank or authorized EEA payment institution. Use a clear payment reference such as 'share capital contribution', 'shareholder loan under agreement dated [date]', or 'paid-in capital increase'. Before remittance, provide the bank with the executed financing instrument, corporate approvals, ownership chart, source-of-funds evidence, remitter-account proof, expected amount and currency, and any applicable foreign-investment or statistical-reporting analysis. For an incorporation or capital-increase account, obtain the bank certificate confirming deposited funds and retain the notarial and commercial-registration records. Convert only the amount needed for euro-denominated capital or operating obligations; retain foreign currency only where supported by the bank's product and treasury controls. Reconcile the bank transfer to the general ledger, shareholder register, debt schedule, tax records, and statutory accounts. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated third parties, anonymous payment platforms, or pooled client-money accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments to eligible European beneficiaries and SWIFT cross-border transfers for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions. A SWIFT MT103 remains a standard customer-payment message, while banks are migrating to ISO 20022 payment messages; retain the bank's payment confirmation, UETR, invoice, contract, beneficiary details, and sanctions-screening record. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, standby letters of credit, documentary collections, or open-account settlement according to counterparty risk and bank availability. For a Commercial LC, define the issuing, advising, and confirming banks; governing rules such as UCP 600 where agreed; documentary requirements; Incoterms; currency; expiry; discrepancy process; and sanctions conditions. For localization services, ordinary service invoices and SEPA or SWIFT payments will usually be more proportionate than documentary trade instruments. Apply beneficiary-name screening, purpose-of-payment accuracy, related-party approval, dual authorization, segregation of duties, invoice matching, and transfer-pricing controls. Spanish banks may delay or reject payments lacking a coherent commercial purpose, complete beneficiary information, or supporting documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, and other bank-supported forward contracts for forecast or committed receivables and payables, documented under a treasury policy and normally confirmed under an ISDA or equivalent bank master agreement.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility or limited delivery markets, subject to bank eligibility, local-market rules, sanctions controls, suitability assessment, and applicable European market-conduct requirements.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for managing recurring currency funding, intercompany loans, or longer-term exposure, subject to counterparty credit limits, collateral terms, valuation controls, and EMIR-related obligations.

Foreign-exchange options, collars, and structured hedges may be used only after documented risk assessment, management approval, appropriateness or suitability procedures where applicable, and full disclosure of premium, leverage, termination, collateral, and accounting consequences.

SEPA and bank spot conversions for ordinary operating flows, with exposure limits, authorized counterparties, segregation of duties, independent rate verification, and monthly hedge-effectiveness and mark-to-market reporting.

Treasury controls should prohibit speculative trading, require hedging of identifiable commercial exposures, maintain hedge-designation and accounting documentation where hedge accounting is intended, and address EMIR clearing, reporting, risk-mitigation, collateral, and record-retention obligations based on the company's classification and transaction profile.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Cuentas Anuales) and management report, deposited at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must approve the accounts within six months of the year-end (calendar-year SL: by 30 June); deposit must be made within one month of approval, making 31 July the outside deadline for calendar-year entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral) barring validity of corporate filings; publication of default in BORME and BOE; fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000; repeated non-filing in dormant companies can lead to administrative strike-off/dissolution by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax self-assessment declaration (Modelo 200, Impuesto sobre Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the close of the six-month period following the tax period; for a calendar-year SL, the deadline is 25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 5%–20% plus late interest; substantive understatement penalties of 50%–150%; administrative garnishment of bank accounts and denial of tax-clearance certificates for unpaid or unobligated filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner declaration / UBO update (hoja de titularidad real) filed at the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven: file within 10 business days after notarial execution of any shareholding or beneficial-ownership change; no separate annual UBO filing is required when ownership is unchanged.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Spanish AML Law 10/2010 sanctions up to EUR 600,000 for serious non-compliance; registry refusal of corporate deeds until the UBO declaration is updated.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if, for two consecutive fiscal years, the SL meets at least two of: total assets exceeding EUR 2,850,000 (approx. USD 3.1 million); net annual turnover exceeding EUR 5,700,000 (approx. USD 6.2 million); average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Audit may also be required at shareholders' request or under exceptional statutory rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC) per Royal Decree 1514/2007, with optional PGC-PYMES framework for qualifying SMEs; individual statutory accounts use Spanish national GAAP, while consolidated accounts apply IFRS as endorsed by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spanish SLs are not required to file a standalone annual UBO confirmation. The beneficial-owner record must be updated and submitted to the Commercial Registry within 10 business days of any notarial share transfer or change in beneficial ownership. The on-site UBO book and annual accounts filing maintain continuous ownership visibility, but the registry filing obligation is event-driven, not calendar-driven.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Libro de Titulares Reales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 330 – 1,300 per year (EUR 300 – 1,200), covering professional registered office, corporate agent and compliance correspondence services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,800 – 6,500 per year (EUR 2,500 – 6,000), typical certified audit fee for a low-risk Spanish SL under ISIC 7490 below the statutory audit thresholds.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% standard rate; 23% for companies with turnover exceeding €1 million; tax incentives including 100% deduction for R&D expenses and innovation premiums

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 - Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically via AEAT (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days after the end of the fiscal year (December 31 for most SL companies)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before tax deductions and incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents report Spanish source income only; adjustments for permanent establishment if applicable
Apply applicable deductions; non-residents may claim treaty benefits
Calculate at 25% or reduced rate; withholdings credited

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Fines of €100-€1,000 per day of delay (max €25,000); criminal prosecution for evasion with fines up to 100% of evaded tax and imprisonment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and DTA application to the withholding agent or Spanish tax authorities for reduced rate application
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10%-25% (treaty dependent, often 10%); Interest: 0%-15% (treaty dependent, often 0% for related parties)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €1 million annual turnover for Local File; €50 million consolidated group turnover for Master File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain adheres to EU Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); requires companies to demonstrate real economic activities, employees, and premises in Spain for tax purposes

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating taxable income or inflating deductible expenses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to 100% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, and restitution orders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors face personal criminal liability, fines, and possible disqualification or travel restrictions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of Modelo 100 within statutory deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines €100 to €1,000 per day of delay, up to €25,000; possible criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and liability for corporate tax obligations; potential imprisonment in aggravated cases

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into non-arm's length transactions without proper documentation or adjustments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of 100% of the tax adjustment; possible restitution of tax benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal liability for fraudulent conduct; fines and disqualification

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining Spanish entity without sufficient substance (employees, operations, decision-making) to justify tax residency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of income; denial of deductions; fines up to €300,000 and potential criminal liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal responsibility for tax liabilities; possible imprisonment for fraudulent tax residency claims
